diagnostic_evidence.quote:
The fully discrete update
  \eqref{eq:fully_discrete_theta_scheme_condensed} is well posed.

issues.failure_explanation:
The bilinear form $a_{n,	heta}(\varphi, \psi)$ involves only the gradients $
abla\varphi$ and $
abla\psi$. For any non-zero constant function $\varphi \equiv c 
eq 0 \in H^1(D)$, $
abla\varphi = \mathbf{0}$, which implies $a_{n,	heta}(\varphi, \varphi) = 0$ while $\|\varphi\|_{H^1(D)} = |c|\sqrt{|D|} > 0$. Therefore, there cannot exist any coercivity constant $\alpha_0 > 0$ such that $a_{n,	heta}(\varphi, \varphi) \ge \alpha_0 \|\varphi\|_{H^1(D)}^2$ for all $\varphi \in H^1(D)$, and coercivity on $H^1(D)$ fails. Consequently, in the absence of boundary conditions, the operator has a non-trivial kernel (constant functions) on $H^1(D)$ and on the continuous discrete space $\mathbb H_h$, meaning the discrete update in (4.3) does not determine $\varphi_h^{n+	heta}$ uniquely, invalidating the well-posedness claim in Corollary 4.3.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify standard boundary conditions for the potential (such as homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions, replacing $H^1(D)$ with $H^1_0(D)$ and $\mathbb H_h$ with $\mathbb H_{h,0}$), which restores coercivity via the Poincaré inequality and guarantees well-posedness.
issues.overall_effect: Coercivity of the bilinear form in Lemma 3.3 and well-posedness (uniqueness) of the potential updates in Corollary 4.3 do not hold as stated on $H^1(D)$ and $\mathbb H_h$.
issues.title: False coercivity on H^1(D) and ill-posedness of potential update due to omitted boundary conditions
issues.why_classification: Restricting the potential to a space with standard Dirichlet boundary conditions is a local, routine fix that preserves all methods, convergence rates, and guarantees, and is already the setup used in the numerical experiments.
